text:
Jordan: Heads-up — customer reported 401s from our Node TS SDK after upgrading to 1.5.0 when running on Edge/SSR (Next.js). Works locally in Node, fails on deployment.
Maria: Oof, any repro steps or logs?
Jordan: Quick repro I have:
1) app imports: `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'`
2) package.json (app):
```
"dependencies": {
  "@redwood/inference": "^1.5.0"
}
```
3) Next app configured for Edge routes (`export const runtime = 'experimental-edge'`)
4) On deploy the SSR route returns 401 with no body. Local Node dev works fine.
Chris: Can you paste the SDK package exports-ish part? bundlers sometimes pick wrong entry.
Jordan: SDK package.json snippet from node_modules:
```
{
  "main": "dist/index.cjs.js",
  "module": "dist/index.esm.js",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/index.esm.js",
      "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js"
    },
    "./runtime": "./dist/runtime.js"
  },
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts"
}
```
Maria: That looks normal. Do you have a lockfile? Checm if there are duplicate versions pulled in.
Jordan: Yes — yarn.lock shows both 1.4.3 and 1.5.0 (transitive via another package that pins 1.4.x). I think bundler duplicated code. I grepped the bundle and found two copies of our `auth.ts` factory.
Sam: Duplicate copies would explain different behavior if one copy is the older code that injects auth differently. Any evidence headers are different?
Jordan: I captured the SSR fetch sidecar logs. Local Node fetch shows `authorization: Bearer <token>`. On Edge bundle request has no Authorization header.
Chris: Edge runtimes often rewrite or strip headers if code path uses `globalThis.fetch` shim or a different client. Could the ESM entry be browser-targeted and drop header logic? Maybe a build-time shim.
Jordan: The `dist/index.esm.js` file contains this at top:
```
// browser fetch wrapper
const f = globalThis.fetch || (() => { throw new Error('fetch missing') });
```
but the header injection lives in `auth.ts` which in 1.4.3 was applied as a middleware on the Node/http client; in 1.5.0 we refactored to apply it within a different module that some bundles prune.
Maria: So two issues: (A) multiple versions -> duplicate modules with different auth wiring, (B) bundler/runtime picks browser ESM entry that expects caller to set header.
Jordan: Repro steps I used:
```
git clone https://git.example/repro-edge-auth
cd repro-edge-auth
yarn
yarn build
yarn start
# hit /api/ssr -> 401
```
Also tried `npm dedupe` and pinning `@redwood/inference@1.5.0` at root but the transitive package still resolves to 1.4.3 for the other dep.
Sam: Good repro. Can you share the minimal bundle trace? which file included the auth logic that drops token?
Jordan: bundle search results:
```
/._next/server/chunks/12345-abc.js -> contains dist/index.esm.js path
/._next/server/chunks/67890-def.js -> contains dist/index.cjs.js path
```
So both copies end up in server bundle.
Chris: Thanks. Workarounds:
- Force single version with a resolution (yarn: `resolutions` / npm overrides)
- Use bundle analyzer to ensure only one copy remains
- As a short-term patch, we can add runtime guard to both variants to reattach token if `process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY` present
Maria: We should also check Node version/edge runtime — customer uses Vercel Edge with Node 18 vs local Node 20. But I think duplicate versions is primary.
Jordan: Customer tried `yarn install --flat` which forced single version and 401 went away.
Sam: Filing internal issue and assigning to eng-platform + devex. Created GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal/issues/987 (link)
support-bot: Created support ticket S-2023-4897, linked to GH issue #987, priority P2, customer impact: production SSR 401s, contact: @support-cs
Chris: Long-term fixes:
- Make package resilient to bundlers: avoid implicit environment differences. E.g., export explicit `//# source` or provide `browser`-safe auth wiring.
- Add an internal check during SDK init: if no auth header found but API_KEY present, attach.
- Improve docs about single-version requirement and add note in migration guide for 1.5.0.
Maria: Also consider publishing a patch that re-exports the same auth module path for both ESM and CJS to reduce duplication risk (or mark files with `sideEffects: false` where safe).
Jordan: Customer accepted pin to 1.4.3 as interim; asked for ETA for fix. Can eng give ETA?
Sam: Eng estimate: hotfix release (1.5.1) next week if we agree on approach. I'll ping eng-runtime and devex for PR.
Chris: I'll open a PR to add a runtime guard + add tests that simulate duplicated module copies (we can run a webpack build with two versions in node_modules and assert headers).
Maria: Thanks team, keep me posted and update the ticket when 1.5.1 is published.
Jordan: Thanks — I’ll relay to customer. :thumbsup:
